 Jared McCain tallied 23 points (8-of-17 FGs), four rebounds, two assists and seven three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 McCain has scored in double figures in four straight games, with Friday’s being the best of the bunch. The Thunder guard shot 7-of-11 from deep against the Clippers, recording season highs in points and three-pointers. McCain will mainly be a “points and triples” option in fantasy leagues, but Oklahoma City’s injuries open the door for him to provide consistent value. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Jared McCain tallied 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 After scoring 19 points off the bench in Saturday’s rout of the Wizards, McCain returned to the Thunder starting lineup on Tuesday. Shooting 4-of-7 from beyond the arc, the third-year guard recorded his third 20-point stat line of the season. While he can be inconsistent, McCain is on a bit of a heater, scoring 21, 19 and 21 points in his last three games. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Tuesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 The Thunder made one change to their starting lineup, with McCain replacing Aday Mara. Portland has only one true big in its lineup, Donovan Clingan, so starting two 7-footers wouldn’t have been the best course of action. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Jared McCain tallied 19 points (8-of-10 FGs, 1-of-1 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and one block over 23 minutes in a blowout win over the Wizards on Saturday. 
 McCain continues to make a significant impact in a versatile role for Oklahoma City this season. He came off the bench in this one and wound up shooting 80 percent from the floor with both of his misses coming from three-point range. He’s scored at least 19 points in back-to-back games and is averaging 25 minutes for the injury-depleted Thunder. They’re back in action with a busy four-game week that includes back-to-back showdowns against the Trail Blazers in addition to road tilts against the Clippers and Kings.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Saturday’s game against the Wizards. 
 The Thunder will start Saturday’s game with a bigger lineup, with Mara starting and Jared McCain coming off the bench. While the production hasn’t been consistent, Mara is worth the risk due to injuries to Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren.

 Guard 
 #3 
 Jared McCain went off for a season-high 21 points (9-of-14 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), five rebounds, four assists and one block over 29 minutes in a one-sided victory over the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 McCain found himself back in Oklahoma City’s starting lineup and delivered an extremely efficient offensive effort, reaching the 20-point plateau for the first time since Oklahoma City’s season-opening win over the Spurs. The 22-year-old has made the most of his increased opportunities for the injury-ravaged Thunder and is worthy of a roster spot in deeper fantasy leagues. Oklahoma City is back in action with a home matchup against the Wizards on Saturday.

 The Oklahoma City Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 The Thunder are going smaller in this game than they did against the Cavs with Aday Mara heads to the bench and Jared McCain returns to the starting lineup. Mara will go back to being a backup center while McCain might get more minutes in this game. If McCain is available, he might be worth grabbing if you need some points and 3’s.

 Although Jared McCain is available for Monday’s game, the Thunder are starting with a bigger lineup. JayWill has replaced him, which should help the Thunder match up better against Cleveland’s Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. 
 Kenrich Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #34 
 Kenrich Williams finished Saturday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers. 
 After totaling 10 points in his first two starts of the season, Williams scored 11 on Saturday. He was most valuable against the Rockets in three-pointers and rebounds, but this performance doesn’t make “Kenny Hustle” a must-add heading into Oklahoma City’s four-game Week 3. Also, with the Thunder playing two games against Cleveland to start the week, it’s fair to wonder whether head coach Mark Daigneault would consider a bigger lineup to match up with Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. If so, Williams or Jared McCain (10/4/2/1) could be headed to the bench.

 Jared McCain tallied 18 points (6-of-14 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Suns. 
 McCain was one of three replacements in the Thunder starting lineup on Monday. With Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/leg) needing surgery, McCain has a good chance of staying a starter for the long haul. He shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc against the Suns and recorded a complete stat line, playing 30 minutes. Like Ajay Mitchell, McCain is a must-add if he’s on the waiver wire.

 The Thunder have three new starters for Monday’s game, and two (McCain and Mitchell) could hold onto those roles for the foreseeable future. Cason Wallace (shoulder) and Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) could miss the rest of the season due to injuries that require surgery. “Kenny Hustle” starts for Chet Holmgren, who is dealing with right patellar tendinitis.

 Isaiah Hartenstein notched 21 points (9-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 16 rebounds, six assists and one steal in Friday’s loss to the Clippers.
 After scoring no more than seven points in any of Oklahoma City’s first five games in November, Hartenstein has scored at least 20 in two straight games. He was outstanding against the Clippers, shooting 90 percent from the field and providing excellent value in points, rebounds and assists. Providing top-100 fantasy value, Hartenstein is rostered in 84 percent of Yahoo leagues. Given Oklahoma City’s frontcourt injuries, those rostering Hartenstein would be better served holding on to him than entertaining a trade after the last two games.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday’s loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-of-26 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
 Gilgeous-Alexander finished with his third 40-point game of the season, but he wishes he’d scored 42 instead of 40. The two-time MVP’s shot as time expired missed the mark, resulting in a 113-112 Clippers victory. After shooting a combined 17-of-42 in two losses to the Trail Blazers, Gilgeous-Alexander was much more efficient on Friday, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. He could be in for another big night to end the week, as the Thunder visit the Kings on Sunday.

 Keaton Wagler produced 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After reaching double figures in each of his first five games, Wagler totaled 13 points on 4-of-13 shooting in the Clippers’ first two games of November. The rookie has gotten back on track, having scored at least 11 points in four straight games. Wagler remains a deep-league option in redraft formats, while dynasty league managers should be excited for the rookie guard’s future.

 Derrick Jones Jr. accounted for 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, one steal, four blocks and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 Thanks mainly to the three-pointers and defensive stats, Jones has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. Against the Thunder, he shot 4-of-7 from beyond the arc and recorded five “stocks” in 29 minutes. This was Jones’ fourth game this season with at least two three-pointers, one steal and one block. Managers needing help in those categories should consider adding Jones ahead of Sunday’s game against the Hornets.

 Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Domantas Sabonis put up 21 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, and a three in the loss on Friday to the Blazers. 
 After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far.
